apps.name: WorkHub
apps.subtitle: Inspections and ECC Daily Hand In
apps.localizedDescription: Native, local-first iPhone inspections and ECC Daily Hand In. Direct Google Drive access, PDF preview, native PDF merging, and ZIP exports. Distributed as an unsigned IPA for sideloading.
apps.versionDescription:
Added: Experimental native rectangular Lock Screen widget showing today's inspection PDF total and ECC/CAMH breakdown from the existing Today dashboard.
Added: App Group sharing of read-only counts, widget reload on saved/live updates, day rollover clearing, and tap-to-open Inspections → Today.
Safety: No credentials or PDF bytes are shared, missing data is never mislabeled zero, and removing an account clears the widget summary.
Build: Manual IPA packaging now checks for the embedded WidgetKit extension. Actual sideload signing/App Group compatibility still needs an on-device test.

versions.localizedDescription:
Added: Experimental native rectangular Lock Screen widget showing today's inspection PDF total and ECC/CAMH breakdown from the existing Today dashboard.
Added: App Group sharing of read-only counts, widget reload on saved/live updates, day rollover clearing, and tap-to-open Inspections → Today.
Safety: No credentials or PDF bytes are shared, missing data is never mislabeled zero, and removing an account clears the widget summary.
Build: Manual IPA packaging now checks for the embedded WidgetKit extension. Actual sideload signing/App Group compatibility still needs an on-device test.

Compression terminology: All three Documents workspaces now use a Compression Level setting labeled Low / Medium / High. Low means less compression and greater retained image quality (usually larger output); High means more compression and generally smaller output. The underlying PDF, Scanner and Images preset identifiers and actual numerical settings are unchanged, with visual order reversed where necessary to preserve the correct direction for existing users. Lossless images retain the existing separate Lossless mode, where no lossy Compression Level is appropriate.
Daily JHA: Adds the same Low / Medium / High Compression Level control to its image imports and photo capture. New JHA Photos library imports are encoded on a background task at the selected dimension/JPEG quality; the existing continuous JHA camera now uses the same level. The 20-image limit remains enforced, imported photos enter the draft in order and are saved together after import. Existing draft photos and generated Daily JHA archives are not recompressed retroactively.
PDF Multi Tool: Replaces the one-photo UIImagePicker with the existing continuous camera workflow used for Daily JHA. Take up to 20 photos (or remaining PDF workspace slots), review the count, Undo Last, Cancel without importing, or tap Done to stage and import the entire batch to the PDF page stack at once. The PDF workspace compression setting is still applied by the existing PDF image-conversion pipeline.
Appearance: Adds the Daily JHA Compression Level preference. Manual Codemagic preflight contains a v0.8.7 regression guard and updated older tests. No GitHub Actions preflight or build added. Full Xcode compilation and device camera interaction require the next user-triggered Codemagic build.

Low means less compression and greater retained image quality (usually larger output); High means more compression and generally smaller output. The underlying PDF, Scanner and Images preset identifiers and actual numerical settings are unchanged, with visual order reversed where necessary to preserve the correct direction for existing users. Lossless images retain the existing separate Lossless mode, where no lossy Compression Level is appropriate.
Daily JHA: Adds the same Low / Medium / High Compression Level control to its image imports and photo capture. New JHA Photos library imports are encoded on a background task at the selected dimension/JPEG quality; the existing continuous JHA camera now uses the same level. The 20-image limit remains enforced, imported photos enter the draft in order and are saved together after import. Existing draft photos and generated Daily JHA archives are not recompressed retroactively.
PDF Multi Tool: Replaces the one-photo UIImagePicker with the existing continuous camera workflow used for Daily JHA. Take up to 20 photos (or remaining PDF workspace slots), review the count, Undo Last, Cancel without importing, or tap Done to stage and import the entire batch to the PDF page stack at once. The PDF workspace compression setting is still applied by the existing PDF image-conversion pipeline.
Appearance: Adds the Daily JHA Compression Level preference. Manual Codemagic preflight contains a v0.8.7 regression guard and updated older tests. No GitHub Actions preflight or build added. Full Xcode compilation and device camera interaction require the next user-triggered Codemagic build.

Improved: The Document Scanner manual four-corner editor now uses inset, draggable blue grips connected to the true crop vertices, keeping fingers approximately 46 points away from the page edge. While dragging, a circular 2.8× magnifier appears on the opposite side with a centered crosshair tracking the actual crop point. Rotation, filters, original-image fallback, perspective correction and manual/auto capture workflows remain intact.
Simplified: Scanner and Daily JHA Clear All actions now show compact centered alerts with only the destructive action and Cancel, without verbose explanations. PDF Multi Tool's clear confirmation likewise drops its redundant paragraph. Removed repetitive instructional text, captions and unused hint toggles from Scanner, Daily JHA, PDF Multi Tool, Inspections, Today, Appearance, icon studios and performance screens.
Preserved: Meaningful status and error messages, camera permission guidance, on-device draft recovery, monthly JHA archive, accessibility hints, OAuth setup instructions and brief security/storage warnings remain available.
Testing: Verify crop-point visibility and loupe placement while dragging every corner, at normal and extreme perspectives, and verify the simplified confirmation dialogs in both Standard and Liquid Glass.

Fixed: Document Scanner now uses the largest plausible page rectangle from multiple Vision observations rather than the first high-confidence inner box. Very small rectangles within safety forms are rejected; manual shutter always works even without a detected page.
Added: A four-corner manual crop editor is shown after taking a scan, on the complete uncropped image. Drag each blue corner to the real paper edge, preview the perspective-straightened result, reset to the full image or the suggested corners, disable cropping, apply a filter, retake, or accept. The final crop is created only after approval and remains local.
Added: Daily JHA Take JHA photos opens a continuous camera session. Capture multiple photos up to the 20-photo total, see the count and last photo, undo a capture, then tap Done to add the whole batch at once. Cancel discards only the new batch. Images are compressed once locally and the existing draft is saved once for the batch.
Preserved: Scanner Next Page remains one-at-a-time, Auto Capture remains single-shot, PDF Multi Tool, Quick Actions, monthly Daily JHA archive, draft recovery and existing export formats remain unchanged.

Fixed: PDF Multi Tool's Add Pages chooser now opens a compact, centered native alert rather than the oversized bottom-positioned confirmation dialog.
Simplified: Removed redundant instructional text; the chooser displays only Select File, Select Image, Take Image (when the camera is available), and Cancel.
Unchanged: The centered Bento-inspired Add Pages panel, image compression at the top, existing Files/Photos/Camera imports, page editing, export and navigation behavior from v0.8.2 are preserved.
Added: Compact Quick Actions on the Today dashboard open Daily JHA, Scanner or PDF Multi Tool without adding another main tab. Quick Actions can be disabled in Appearance → Inspections layout.
Added: Recover unfinished Daily JHA, Document Scanner and PDF Multi Tool drafts across app relaunches. Store photos, scanned pages and imported PDF source files locally in Application Support, along with order, selection, rotations and output names; clearing a draft does not delete saved dailies.
Added: Daily JHA PDFs generated successfully are archived by their hand-in date into monthly groups. Daily Hand In → Monthly Daily JHA archive lets you preview each saved daily or combine all saved dailies for a chosen month into a single chronological PDF (for example, October 2026 Dailies.pdf). Only the JHA PDF is included; Harness and Lift inspection PDFs remain separate.
Improved: Settings overview is more concise, advanced module visibility/layout presets are collapsed by default, and previously available customization remains accessible.
Note: The local monthly archive begins capturing successfully generated JHAs from this update onward; old documents saved elsewhere are not automatically imported.

Fixed: Bottom navigation now occupies its own layout row instead of an inset over the native TabView, keeping page content above the dock. Scroll clearance is inserted into Forms, Lists, and ScrollViews, including Settings, Appearance, Inspections, Daily JHA, Scanner, PDF Multi Tool, diagnostics, and icon studios, so final controls can be scrolled into view.
Changed: Standard-mode Inspections and Documents subtabs now use tap-only controls without iOS 26 drag-to-select behavior. Liquid Glass keeps its native segmented picker.
Added: Standard bottom navigation now supports sliding across tabs and releasing on a destination as well as tapping individual tabs.
Redesigned: PDF Multi Tool shows a centered Add Pages card when empty, with Files/Photos/Camera choices and image compression retained at the top. After import, a compact Add More Pages button appears above the page workspace. Existing import/export and draft state remain unchanged.
Testing: Check last-row access across all major screens, tap-only Standard subtabs and main dock dragging, plus PDF Multi Tool in empty and populated states.
Refined: Empty PDF Multi Tool workspace now uses a narrower, centered dashed-outline upload panel inspired by BentoPDF. The entire panel opens WorkHub's existing Files/Photos/Camera chooser, with a compact blue Add Pages CTA; image compression stays separate at the top. This is a native tap target, not a misleading drag-and-drop promise.

Fixed: Standard interface subtabs no longer show an extra rectangular material backing behind the rounded segmented control.
Fixed: Documents now shows PDF Multi Tool or Document Scanner page title above its PDF Multi Tool / Scanner segmented switch, matching Inspections.
Preserved: PDF/Scanner draft state remains mounted during subtab switches. Navigation, scanning workflow, local PDF creation and existing appearance options remain unchanged.
Added: Manual document scanning now shows a live blue four-corner outline around detected page edges before the shutter is pressed; automatic mode uses the same guide. The outline tracks perspective with camera framing, never triggers a photo in manual mode, and clears for review/retake. The captured photo still receives its own high-resolution crop detection for final output.

Fixed: Standard navigation is now solid and bottom-attached instead of a floating translucent capsule. Liquid Glass retains the separate floating dock; both share a reserved bottom safe-area layout to reduce obscured controls.
Improved: Inspections and Documents subtabs now use shared consistent height and padding.
Changed: Document Scanner uses a one-page camera flow with manual shutter or optional stable-edge Auto Capture (off by default), on-device perspective correction and page review with filters. After each page, select Next Page to resume scanning; automatic capture cannot repeatedly photograph the same page.
Retained: Scanner grid/list, 40-page cap, rotation, reorder, local verified PDF exports, share/save, compression choices and PDF Multi Tool handoff.
Testing: Built for manual Codemagic compilation and on-device review; confirm scanner crop and both navigation modes on iPhone.

New: Documents replaces the PDF Multi Tool main-tab title while preserving its saved tab identifier, tab order and existing PDF workspace. Documents contains two subtabs: PDF Multi Tool and Document Scanner; independently hide either module or set the preferred subtab in Appearance.
New: Native Apple VisionKit document scanner captures multiple pages from the camera, with automatic page-edge detection, perspective correction, interactive crop and filters before saving a scan. Return to the scanner to add more pages.
New: Review scanned pages in configurable grid or list form, preview/zoom, reorder, rotate left or right, remove individual scans, and Clear All with confirmation. Image processing is bounded to 40 pages and three configurable capture quality presets. Scans are prepared offline on device; no Google Drive upload.
New: Export an image-based PDF using Original proportions, Letter or A4 page sizing. Validate that the generated PDF opens and that its page count matches the scan. Save to Files or share with the system share sheet, or send the PDF directly into PDF Multi Tool for further editing. Old local scan exports are cleaned after seven days; already saved/shared copies remain untouched. Searchable OCR isn't included in this release.
Improved: Appearance now groups Look & feel, Navigation, Workspace layouts, visible modules, presets and reset more clearly; Liquid Glass controls live on a focused detail page. Document Scanner has its own appearance settings for layout, thumbnail size, counters, tips, capture quality and PDF paper size. Existing PDF Multi Tool appearance settings keep their previous keys.
Improved: Liquid Glass and Standard use visibly different navigation styling with a floating dock and adjustable WorkHub glass clarity where iOS 26 supports it.
Improved: Shared thumbnail preview-eye overlays and rotate-left/right menus across PDF Multi Tool, Daily JHA and Document Scanner. JHA supports rotating within its full-screen preview.
Safety: Google credential management stays tucked into advanced account settings. Scanner results never upload automatically; PDF exports are created on device. Existing inspection cache, JHA generation and PDF original files are untouched.
Build: Codemagic is the manual primary builder; GitHub Actions remains a manual-only backup.

Improved safety: Removed the prominent red Disconnect and delete Google credentials button from Settings. Move local account removal to Settings → Account & security → Advanced connection actions, hidden behind a collapsed disclosure and a separate destructive confirmation.
Clarified: Disconnecting signs out and deletes manually saved OAuth credentials from iPhone Keychain, and clears the local Google Drive inspection cache (including downloaded inspection PDFs). It never deletes Google Drive originals, the Google account, or already exported JHA/PDF files.
Added: Settings → Appearance → Interface & navigation lets you choose Standard or enhanced Liquid Glass (iOS 26+), independently of light/dark mode and accent color. Live visual preview demonstrates the setting.
Added: In Liquid Glass mode, retain Apple's native floating iPhone tab bar and let it shrink while scrolling down and expand when scrolling back up. Accessible native tabs, hidden modules, saved tab order and draft state are retained.
Improved: Native iOS 26 glass styling for the inspection search field, PDF Add Pages action, Daily JHA Generate action and select navigation controls. The rest of the content stays clean to preserve readability and minimize GPU/memory impact.
Compatible: iOS 17–25 continue using standard materials; existing users keep their established styling until opting in. Restore Appearance Defaults reverts the interface style to Standard.
Added: CI regression checks for hidden/confirmed account removal, interface preferences, native tab behavior, and backward-compatible appearance.

Added: Tap any added image or its filename in Field → Daily JHA to open a large, full-screen JHA photo preview without generating the daily package first.
Added: Pinch-to-zoom up to 6×, drag to pan when zoomed, and double-tap to zoom in or reset. Previous/next controls browse all JHA photos in their current draft order, with an image counter and a Done button.
Improved: The preview respects each photo's existing 90° rotation without creating a second full-resolution rotated JPEG. Only the selected JPEG is decoded off the main UI thread, and its preview image is released when the viewer closes.
Safe: Preview is read-only—JHA photo order, rotation, output, Drive inspections and previously exported documents are unchanged. Clear All also dismisses any selected preview.
Added: CI regression checks for tap-to-preview, photo order/navigation, zoom handling, rotation, and release of the loaded preview image.
Unchanged: Daily JHA generation, photo import/reordering, Clear All, PDF Multi Tool, performance diagnostics, app icons and automatic IPA publishing.

Added: Daily JHA now includes a visible Clear All button in the JHA photos section. It asks for confirmation before removing every attached camera/library JHA photo and resetting the page to today's date, default ZIP output option, and empty progress/error/output state.
Fixed: Clearing the Daily JHA also invalidates in-progress Photos picker imports so images selected before the reset cannot unexpectedly reappear after a slow PhotoKit load finishes.
Improved: Reordering, deleting, rotating, or adding JHA images invalidates a previously generated output from the page, preventing accidental reuse after the draft changes.
Safe: Clear All is disabled while Daily JHA is generating. Already exported files and Google Drive inspection caches remain intact; app appearance settings are unaffected.
Added: CI regression checks for confirmation, draft reset, and in-flight photo selection invalidation.
Unchanged: PDF Multi Tool, Daily JHA generation and live ECC inspection fetching, performance diagnostics, icon customization and automatic IPA publishing.

Improved: PDF Multi Tool now prepares preview source PDF documents off the main UI thread, preventing synchronous PDF document parsing in PDFView.makeUIView during sheet presentation.
Improved: PDFKit previews explicitly clear their PDF document reference on sheet teardown, and the SwiftUI preview releases its document after dismissal to reduce retained pages and renderer memory across multiple previews.
Improved: The thumbnail renderer retains at most one open source PDF document rather than one per imported file, while continuing to use its existing bounded low-resolution image cache. Source documents are released when leaving the PDF workspace or closing a preview.
Added: A PDF preview-loaded event and preview-dismissed event to opt-in UI responsiveness reports for more precise before/after PDFKit and memory measurements.
Added: A CI regression test verifying the preview load/teardown lifecycle and bounded thumbnail document retention.
Unchanged: Original PDFs, page order and rotations, export quality, selection, Google Drive inspection caches, Daily JHA and app appearance. Existing thumbnail images remain cached.

Added: Performance Testing → Live Diagnostics now attributes display-link stalls and sampled memory changes to the active WorkHub tab or Field section, rather than showing only aggregate worst-gap and peak-memory numbers.
Added: A bounded timeline of tab changes and PDF workspace actions (import, preview, export and clear), with the twelve largest callback gaps and up to twenty-four recent actions in each shareable report. Only screen categories, counts, timestamps and memory are recorded—never inspection names or PDF filenames.
Added: Per-screen counts of slow callbacks, approximate missed callbacks, worst gap and sampled resident memory entry/peak/last, so Navigation and PDF-specific spikes can be compared directly.
Improved: Previous v0.7.3 diagnostic history remains readable; attribution is opt-in and runs only during the existing 20-second UI monitor. Correlation with a screen/action is not a proof of root cause.
Added: Regression tests verifying per-screen attribution and sampled memory accounting.
Unchanged: Existing PDF and thumbnail cache behavior, inspection caching, Daily JHA, performance microbenchmarks, icons and automatic IPA feed publishing.

Added: Settings → Performance Testing → Startup, UI smoothness & real PDFs, a new live diagnostic suite complementing repeatable benchmarks.
Added: An optional 20-second CADisplayLink measurement of main-run-loop callback intervals, 95th-percentile and worst callback gap, intervals over a 60 Hz target, approximate missed callbacks and sampled peak resident memory while navigating across WorkHub.
Added: Startup diagnostics for WorkHub initialization to first root view appearance, Google authentication restore duration and existing inspection metadata catalog disk loading. These are labeled as approximations, not full operating-system cold-launch instrumentation.
Added: Choose a PDF from Files to measure actual read-only copy, PDFKit open, bounded thumbnail rendering, and temporary three-page subset export. Supports PDFs up to 120 MB and 200 pages; never changes or retains the original document or filename.
Added: On-device diagnostic history with shareable aggregate text reports and cancellation; detailed results distinguish callback timing from GPU FPS and sampled memory from actual absolute peaks.
Added: Regression tests for frame timing and callback gap calculations.
Unchanged: Inspection search, Daily JHA, caches, PDF Multi Tool, Home Screen icon choices and automatic workhub-ios-feed IPA distribution.

Improved: WorkHub's indexed inspection search now performs fuzzy word matching only once per unique normalized term in the catalog, instead of repeating the same edit-distance checks across thousands of PDF names and shared date aliases.
Improved: Retains phrase matching, partial words, typo tolerance, filename-priority sorting, date aliases, and original result counts. One-time search index construction now deduplicates vocabulary words; interactive queries reuse those matches.
Added: Extended exact-result compatibility tests against the original search logic across 40 queries, including punctuation, accents, misspellings and date formats.
Improved: Benchmark reports identify the number of unique vocabulary words for indexed search to make device performance measurements easier to interpret.
Unchanged: Inspection metadata, cached PDFs, Google Drive updates, Daily JHA, PDF Multi Tool, app icons, and the feed distribution workflow.

Improved: Inspection Browse fuzzy search now reuses prepared normalized filenames and date aliases across keystrokes instead of repeatedly parsing and formatting every inspection date for every search.
Improved: The index is prepared off the main UI thread and refreshed when local inspection metadata changes, preserving fuzzy matching, search totals, filename-first ranking and result limits.
Added: Performance Testing separates one-time search preparation from warmed indexed search to make before/after performance comparisons meaningful.
Added: Automated regression checks compare all search result counts and ordering against the previous implementation across 24 queries, including date variants, typos and accented filenames.
Unchanged: Inspection metadata and PDF storage, Daily JHA, PDF Multi Tool, Home Screen icon options and the sideloader feed workflow.

Added: Settings → Testing & diagnostics → Performance Testing, a fully on-device benchmark lab for measuring app performance without altering inspections or documents.
Added: Repeatable synthetic inspection-index benchmarks for daily summaries, fuzzy search, cached metadata encode/decode and count lookups, plus 12-page PDFKit opening, thumbnail rendering, merge/export and temporary storage I/O.
Added: Optional read-only benchmarks of the device's existing cached inspection metadata. No Google Drive API requests, downloads, or modifications are made.
Added: App memory snapshots, thermal/Low Power Mode indicators, median/min/max timings, fast (3 samples) and detailed (5 samples) runs, cancellation, locally saved history and shareable text reports.
Improved: Previous-run comparisons support checking regressions after IPA updates. Test workloads use isolated synthetic data and temporary files, and production caches are left untouched.
Unchanged: All inspection workflows, Daily JHA, PDF Multi Tool, icon customization and automatic AltStore/SideStore publishing.

Fixed: WorkHub no longer falsely reports that changing the app icon failed when the iPhone Home Screen changes but UIApplication.alternateIconName remains stale.
Fixed: Selection now persists after the UIKit completion handler reports success, including when restoring the original icon, so the correct gallery checkmark survives relaunch.
Improved: A valid stored successful selection takes precedence over a stale iOS icon-name getter; first-launch fallback still uses the actual getter when there is no saved choice.
Added: Regression tests for stale nil/old system values, successful changes, restoring Original WorkHub, and genuine iOS errors.
Unchanged: All 12 alternate icon designs, original AppIcon, inspection workflows, Daily JHA, PDF tools, and automatic sideloader feed publishing.

Updated: Redesigned all twelve alternate WorkHub iPhone app icons with genuinely distinct central silhouettes at Home Screen size, rather than near-identical logo recolors.
Updated: Each option has a construction or inspection identity (hardhat, blueprint, shield, lift, harness, WH monogram, checklist, tools, documents, gear, fieldwork) and consistent WorkHub blue, white and orange palette.
Improved: Smaller-size visual differentiation tests ensure all twelve choices remain distinct even in a 60px Home Screen preview.
Unchanged: The original primary WorkHub icon, icon identifiers and restore-original action remain intact. Inspections, Daily JHA, PDF Multi Tool and cached data are unchanged.

Updated: Twelve Home Screen icon alternatives now retain the original WorkHub hardhat, checklist and orange arc, with distinct engineering, construction and framing details.
Fixed: The new Original WorkHub action explicitly restores the default app icon via the iOS nil icon name.
Fixed: Icon-selection feedback checks the actual UIKit icon (including after foregrounding), waits for the operating system to apply the change and reports real failures instead of treating a tapped preview as applied.
Improved: Alternative icon system identifiers are unchanged, preserving selections across upgrades.
Unchanged: Inspection dashboard icons, Google Drive, Daily JHA, inspection caches and PDF Multi Tool.

Added: Choose WorkHub's actual iPhone Home Screen app icon from 13 visual options under Settings → Customize WorkHub → Home Screen app icon.
Added: Twelve original 1024px alternate icons with different artwork: Blueprint, Hardhat, Night Shift, Safety Shield, Scissor Lift, Fall Protection, WH Monogram, Inspection, Toolbox, Documents, Industrial, and Fieldwork, plus the original Classic.
Added: Large live icon previews, selected-state badges, and system-level icon changing through iOS's supported setAlternateIconName API.
Improved: Clear feedback if a sideloading/signing method disables alternate icons or the icon change fails; WorkHub never falsely reports a change.
Verified: GitHub Actions checks every generated image and all alternate registrations in the production IPA's Info.plist.
Unchanged: Inspection dashboard icon customization, Google Drive, Daily Hand In, offline cache, and PDF Multi Tool.

Fixed: Missing Lift pictograms on the Today dashboard and source rows; removed the unsupported SF Symbol that rendered blank.
Updated: Harness now defaults to a custom safety-harness drawing, while Lift defaults to a recognizable scissor-lift drawing instead of a generic checklist/unsupported symbol.
Added: Appearance → Inspections layout → Today dashboard icon designs, with 10 genuinely different pictograms for Harness and 10 for Lift, each independently selectable with a live visual preview.
Improved: Native SwiftUI vector equipment artwork remains sharp in any appearance mode; unsupported optional system symbols gracefully fall back to an equipment icon instead of disappearing.
Improved: Removed misleading action arrows from noninteractive Today summary cards.
Unchanged: Inspection counts, Today refresh, ECC Daily Hand In, offline cache and PDF Multi Tool behavior remain the same.

Fixed: Daily Hand In always checks current-day ECC Harness and Lift inspection folders live before generating PDFs, even when the local 24-hour cache previously showed no submissions.
Updated: The same lightweight live check refreshes today's PDF metadata and folder counts across ECC and CAMH, and saves the changes for Browse and the Today dashboard.
Improved: Subsequent inspection-cache updates fetch only today's mutable date plus any days that need one final post-midnight check; historical completed days are never scanned again.
Improved: Existing on-device inspection catalogs migrate automatically to the finalized-day watermark without deleting saved PDFs or triggering a complete historical rescan.
Updated: Inspection cache settings explain incremental refresh and permanent past-day retention.
Unchanged: Downloaded ECC inspection PDFs remain stored on-device, and Daily Hand In's ZIP/clipboard workflow, PDF Multi Tool and appearance settings remain intact.

privacy.name: Camera
privacy.usageDescription: Scan paper documents and capture photos for PDF Multi Tool and ECC Daily JHA.
